title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Minutes of the National Conference on Bankruptcy Trial Work of Courts
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the

"Minutes of the National Conference on Bankruptcy Trial Work of Courts"

Fa [2018] No. 53

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The "Minutes of the National Conference on Bankruptcy Trial Work of Courts" are hereby issued to you for earnest compliance and implementation.

March 4, 2018

Minutes of the National Conference on Bankruptcy Trial Work of Courts

To implement the requirements set forth in the Report of the 19th National Congress of the Communist Party of China on implementing the new development concept, building a modern economic system, closely focusing on the main line of high-quality development, serving and safeguarding supply-side structural reform, fully leveraging the positive role of the bankruptcy trial work of People's Courts in improving the rescue and exit mechanisms for socialist market economy entities, and providing stronger judicial guarantees for securing a decisive victory in building a moderately prosperous society in all respects, the Supreme People's Court held the National Conference on Bankruptcy Trial Work of Courts in Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province, on December 25, 2017. Representatives from the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and from Intermediate People's Courts with established bankruptcy trial divisions, attended the conference. Through earnest discussion, the attending representatives reached consensus on the main issues involved in the bankruptcy trial work of People's Courts. These minutes are hereby recorded as follows:

I. General Requirements for Bankruptcy Trials

The conference held that People's Courts must be guided by Xi Jinping's economic thought on socialism with Chinese characteristics for a new era, deeply understand the significant importance of the rule of law in bankruptcy to securing a decisive victory in building a moderately prosperous society in all respects, and carry out bankruptcy trial work with more robust measures, providing stronger judicial guarantees for sustained and healthy economic and social development. The general requirements for bankruptcy trial work for the current period and the near future are:

Firstly, to leverage the function of bankruptcy trials to help build a modern economic system. People's Courts should achieve resource reallocation through bankruptcy work, make good use of the favorable opportunity of significant adjustments in rights and interests, operations and management, assets, technology, etc., during enterprise bankruptcy, handle different types of enterprises through classified disposal, mobilize, allocate, and coordinate production factors such as technology, capital, labor, and human resources effectively, and promote high-quality and efficient development of the real economy and industrial system.

Secondly, to focus on serving the construction of a new economic system and improve the rescue and exit mechanisms for market entities. Legal means of reorganization and compromise should be fully utilized to achieve effective rescue of market entities, helping enterprises improve quality and efficiency; liquidation means should be used to prompt the timely exit of enterprises and production capacity that have lost operational value, achieving survival of the fittest, thereby improving the rescue and exit mechanisms for socialist market entities.

Thirdly, to improve the working mechanisms for bankruptcy trials, maximizing the value of bankruptcy trials. The four working mechanisms for bankruptcy trials — identification of enterprises for bankruptcy reorganization, coordination between government and courts, communication of case information, and lawful and orderly balancing of interests — should be further improved to promote the benign operation of bankruptcy trial work and demonstrate the systemic value and social responsibility of bankruptcy trial work.

Fourthly, to improve the orderly connection between enforcement and bankruptcy work, promoting the resolution of "difficulties in enforcement." Bankruptcy trials should be regarded as an important link that both connects with and is relatively independent from case filing, adjudication, and enforcement. The promoting function of bankruptcy trials in resolving accumulated enforcement cases should be fully leveraged, obstacles to the transfer from enforcement to bankruptcy should be eliminated, and effective ways to solve the "difficulties in enforcement" should be explored from the judicial working mechanism.

II. Professionalization of Bankruptcy Trials

Professionalization of trials is a key link in achieving substantive progress in bankruptcy trial work. People's Courts at all levels should vigorously strengthen the professionalization of bankruptcy trials, striving to achieve professionalization of trial institutions, professionalization of trial teams, standardization of trial procedures, standardization of adjudication rules, and scientific performance evaluation.

1. Promote the professionalization of bankruptcy trial institutions. Intermediate People's Courts located in provincial capitals and cities specifically designated in the state plan should promptly establish Liquidation and Bankruptcy Trial Divisions in accordance with the Supreme People's Court's "Work Plan on Establishing Liquidation and Bankruptcy Trial Divisions in Intermediate People's Courts" (Fa [2016] No. 209). Other courts at all levels may decide to establish Liquidation and Bankruptcy Trial Divisions or specialized collegiate panels based on the actual needs of their local work, and cultivate professional judges familiar with liquidation and bankruptcy trials to meet the needs of bankruptcy trial work.

2. Rationally allocate trial tasks. The trial tasks of People's Courts at all levels should be rationally allocated based on factors such as the number of bankruptcy cases, the difficulty of cases, and trial force. For bankruptcy cases with complex creditor-debtor relationships and high trial difficulty, High People's Courts may explore a jurisdiction system based on the principle of centralized jurisdiction by Intermediate People's Courts, with jurisdiction by Basic People's Courts as an exception; for bankruptcy cases with simple creditor-debtor relationships and low trial difficulty, they may be mainly under the jurisdiction of Basic People's Courts, which can efficiently conclude them through expedited trial procedures.

3. Establish a scientific performance evaluation system. The performance evaluation system for liquidation and bankruptcy trial work should be improved as soon as possible. Performance evaluation standards should be determined on the basis of full respect for the laws of judicial work, avoiding simply comparing the handling of liquidation and bankruptcy cases with ordinary cases, treating them as equivalent, or evaluating them on the same basis.

III. Improvement of the Administrator System

Administrators are the main drivers of bankruptcy proceedings and the specific executors of bankruptcy affairs. The ability and quality of administrators not only affect the quality of bankruptcy trial work but also relate to the fate and future development of bankrupt enterprises. It is necessary to accelerate the improvement of the administrator system, vigorously enhance the professional competence and practice ability of administrators, and strengthen the guarantee of administrators' performance of duties and effective supervision, providing a strong institutional guarantee for improving enterprise operations and optimizing industrial structure.

4. Improve the structure of the administrator team. People's Courts should guide intermediary institutions listed in the administrator roster to adopt appropriate methods to absorb personnel with professional technical knowledge and enterprise management capabilities to join the administrator team, promote a more reasonable internal structure of the administrator team, and fully leverage and enhance the important role of administrators in areas such as enterprise disease diagnosis and resource integration.

5. Explore cross-regional practice of administrators. In addition to selecting administrators from the local roster, courts in various regions may also explore the appointment of administrators from the rosters of other provinces or cities, ensuring that the best administrator can be selected for major bankruptcy cases. If two or more qualified intermediary institutions request to jointly serve as administrators for the same bankruptcy case, the People's Court may permit this after reviewing and confirming that it meets the requirements of voluntary negotiation, complementary advantages, consistency of rights and obligations, and is genuinely necessary.

6. Implement hierarchical management of administrators. High People's Courts, or Intermediate People's Courts that compile their own administrator rosters, may comprehensively consider factors such as the administrator's professional level, work experience, professional ethics, work performance, and diligence, reasonably determine the administrator's grade, implement hierarchical management of administrators, and conduct regular evaluations. For bankruptcy cases with a small amount of debtor property and simple creditor-debtor relationships, the administrator may be appointed from the corresponding grade of administrators by random methods such as rotation, lot drawing, or number-drawing.

7. Establish a working mechanism for competitive selection of administrators. A competitive mechanism may be introduced in bankruptcy cases for the selection of administrators to improve the quality of bankruptcy management. For bankruptcy cases of listed companies, bankruptcy cases with significant local impact, or bankruptcy cases with complex creditor-debtor relationships and a large number of creditors, employees, and interested parties, the administrator should generally be lawfully selected through competitive means when appointing the administrator.

8. Reasonably define the scope of functions of the court and the administrator. People's Courts should support and ensure that administrators lawfully perform their duties and shall not make decisions on behalf of the administrator that should be made by the administrator itself. Administrators shall lawfully manage and dispose of debtor property, prudently decide on the debtor's internal management affairs, and shall not transfer all or part of their duties to others.

9. Further implement the duties of the administrator. In a self-managed reorganization proceeding by the debtor, the People's Court shall urge the administrator to formulate specific systems for supervising the debtor. During the supervision period stipulated in the reorganization plan, the administrator shall represent the debtor in participating in litigation or arbitration activities that have been initiated but not yet concluded before the start of the supervision period. After the reorganization or compromise proceeding is converted into a bankruptcy liquidation proceeding, the administrator shall continue to perform the duties of the administrator in accordance with the bankruptcy liquidation proceeding.

10. Utilize the incentive and constraint role of administrator remuneration. People's Courts may determine the payment method of administrator remuneration based on the specific circumstances of the bankruptcy case, leveraging the positive role of administrator remuneration in incentivizing and constraining administrators to perform their duties diligently. Administrator remuneration should generally be paid in installments based on the progress of the bankruptcy case trial and the administrator's performance of duties. For bankruptcy cases with simple facts and short duration, the administrator's remuneration may be paid in a lump sum after the conclusion of the bankruptcy proceeding.

11. Regulation of expenses for other personnel hired by the administrator. If the administrator hires enterprise management personnel with the permission of the People's Court, or if it is genuinely necessary for the administrator to hire other social intermediary institutions or personnel to handle professional tasks such as major litigation, arbitration, enforcement, or auditing, and the required expenses need to be included in the bankruptcy expenses, approval from the creditors' meeting shall be obtained.

12. Promote the establishment of a comprehensive security system for bankruptcy expenses. Courts in various regions should actively seek support from financial departments, or adopt methods such as extracting a certain proportion from the remuneration of administrators in other bankruptcy cases, to promote the establishment of a bankruptcy expense security fund and establish a long-term mechanism for bankruptcy expense security, solving the problem of affecting the initiation of bankruptcy proceedings due to insufficient debtor property to cover bankruptcy expenses.

13. Support and guide the establishment of administrator associations. People's Courts shall support, guide, and promote social intermediary institutions and individuals listed in the local administrator roster to establish administrator associations, strengthen the management and constraints on administrators, protect the lawful rights and interests of administrators, and gradually form standardized, stable, and self-disciplined industry organizations, ensuring that the administrator team develops both vigorously and in a standardized and orderly manner.

IV. Bankruptcy Reorganization

The conference held that the reorganization system embodies the rescue function of bankruptcy law and represents the development trend of modern bankruptcy law. People's Courts at all levels should attach great importance to reorganization work, properly adjudicate enterprise reorganization cases, rescue troubled enterprises through market-oriented and law-based means, and continuously improve the rescue mechanism for socialist market entities.

14. Identification and review of enterprises for reorganization. The object of bankruptcy reorganization should be troubled enterprises with rescue value and possibility; for zombie enterprises, market exit should be decisively achieved through bankruptcy liquidation. When reviewing a reorganization application, if the People's Court can determine, based on factors such as the debtor's asset status, technology and processes, production and sales, and industry prospects, that the debtor clearly lacks reorganization value and rescue possibility, it shall rule to reject the application.

15. Hearing procedures for reorganization cases. For reorganization cases involving complex creditor-debtor relationships, large debt scales, or those involving listed companies, the People's Court may organize a hearing for the applicant and the respondent when reviewing the reorganization application. Creditors, contributors, reorganization investors, and other interested parties may also participate in the hearing with the permission of the People's Court. The hearing period shall not be counted within the review period for the reorganization application.

16. Formulation of reorganization plans and communication and coordination. People's Courts shall strengthen communication with the administrator or the debtor, guide them to analyze the reasons for the debtor's difficulties, formulate a draft reorganization plan in a targeted manner, prompt the enterprise to regain profitability, and improve the success rate of reorganization. People's Courts shall establish communication and coordination mechanisms with the government to assist the administrator or the debtor in solving difficulties and problems in the formulation of the draft reorganization plan.

17. Review and approval of reorganization plans. Reorganization is not limited to debt reduction and financial adjustment; the focus of reorganization is to maintain the going-concern value of the enterprise. When reviewing a reorganization plan, in addition to legality review, the People's Court shall also review whether the business plan therein is feasible. If the business plan in the reorganization plan for the enterprise to regain profitability is feasible, the voting procedure is lawful, and the content does not harm the settlement interests of opponents in each voting group, the People's Court shall rule to approve the reorganization plan within thirty days from the date of receiving the application.

18. Conditions for coercive approval of draft reorganization plans. People's Courts shall prudently apply Article 87, Paragraph 2 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law and shall not abuse the power of coercive approval. If coercive approval of a draft reorganization plan is genuinely necessary, in addition to complying with Article 87, Paragraph 2 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, if the creditors are divided into multiple groups, at least one group must have already passed the draft reorganization plan, and the settlement benefits that opponents in each voting group can obtain shall not be lower than the benefits obtainable under the bankruptcy liquidation proceeding.

19. Conditions and procedures for changes during the execution of reorganization plans. The debtor shall strictly execute the reorganization plan. However, due to special circumstances such as national policy adjustments or legal amendments, making the original reorganization plan unenforceable, the debtor or the administrator may apply once to change the reorganization plan. If the creditors' meeting resolves to agree to the change of the reorganization plan, it shall submit an application to the People's Court for approval within ten days from the date of adoption of the resolution. If the creditors' meeting resolves not to agree or the People's Court does not approve the change application, the People's Court shall, upon the request of the administrator or an interested party, rule to terminate the execution of the reorganization plan and declare the debtor bankrupt.

20. Re-voting and ruling approval after changes to reorganization plans. If the People's Court rules to agree to change the reorganization plan, the debtor or the administrator shall submit a new reorganization plan within six months. The changed reorganization plan shall be submitted to the creditor groups and contributor groups that are adversely affected by the change in the reorganization plan for voting. The procedures for voting, applying for People's Court approval, and the People's Court ruling on whether to approve shall be the same as those for the original reorganization plan.

21. Guarantees for normal production and operation of reorganized enterprises. After enterprise reorganization, the investment subject, equity structure, corporate governance model, and business methods often undergo fundamental changes compared to the original enterprise. People's Courts shall, through strengthening communication and coordination with the government, assist the reorganized enterprise in repairing its credit record and obtaining tax preferences lawfully, so as to facilitate the reorganized enterprise in resuming normal production and operation.

22. Explore the connection between out-of-court restructuring and in-court reorganization systems. Before an enterprise enters the reorganization proceeding, creditors, debtors, contributors, and other interested parties may first negotiate out of court to formulate a restructuring plan. After the reorganization proceeding is initiated, a draft reorganization plan may be formulated based on the restructuring plan and submitted to the People's Court for review and approval according to law.

V. Bankruptcy Liquidation

The conference held that bankruptcy liquidation, as an important part of the bankruptcy system, has the direct effect of eliminating backward production capacity and optimizing the allocation of market resources. For debtors lacking rescue value and possibility, the creditor-debtor relationships should be comprehensively cleared through the bankruptcy liquidation proceeding in a timely manner, social resources should be reallocated, the quality and level of effective social supply should be improved, and the guiding role of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law in the development of the market economy should be enhanced.

23. Conditions for declaration of bankruptcy. After the People's Court accepts an application for bankruptcy liquidation, if no application for reorganization or compromise is submitted at the first creditors' meeting, the administrator shall promptly apply to the People's Court for a declaration of bankruptcy after verifying claims and conducting necessary audit and asset appraisal. After the People's Court accepts an application for bankruptcy compromise or reorganization, if the debtor meets the statutory reasons for being declared bankrupt, the People's Court shall declare the debtor bankrupt according to law.

24. Procedures for declaration of bankruptcy and restrictions on conversion. If a relevant entity applies to the People's Court for a declaration of bankruptcy, the People's Court shall make a ruling declaring bankruptcy and issue a public notice within seven days from the date of receiving the application. Once the debtor is declared bankrupt, it may not be converted back into a reorganization proceeding or compromise proceeding.

25. Exercise and restriction of the rights of secured creditors. In bankruptcy liquidation and bankruptcy compromise proceedings, a creditor with a security interest in specific property of the debtor may at any time claim against the administrator for priority satisfaction from the realization of that specific property. The administrator shall promptly realize the property and shall not refuse on grounds such as requiring a resolution of the creditors' meeting. This does not apply if separate disposal of the secured property would reduce the value of other bankruptcy property and thus overall disposal is necessary.

26. Disposal of bankruptcy property. Disposal of bankruptcy property shall be based on the principle of maximizing value, while also taking into account disposal efficiency. People's Courts shall actively explore more effective methods and channels for disposing of bankruptcy property, maximizing the realization rate of bankruptcy property. If the proceeds from an auction are estimated to be insufficient to cover the evaluation and auction expenses, or if the auction is unsuccessful, the property may be disposed of by appraised sale or distribution in kind upon a resolution of the creditors' meeting. If the plan for appraised sale or distribution in kind is still not passed by the creditors' meeting after two votes, the matter shall be decided by a ruling of the People's Court.

27. Enterprise bankruptcy and protection of employees' rights and interests. In bankruptcy proceedings, labor relations shall be properly handled according to law, the mechanism for guaranteeing payment of back wages for employees shall be improved, and the right to survival of employees shall be protected according to law. For employee claims advanced by a third party, they shall generally be satisfied according to the nature of the advanced employee claims; for claims advanced by a wage protection fund, they shall be satisfied in the order specified in Article 113, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law. The housing provident fund arrears of the debtor shall be satisfied according to the nature of the debtor's wage arrears to employees.

28. Principles and order for satisfaction of bankruptcy claims. For claims for which the law does not clearly stipulate the order of satisfaction, the People's Court may reasonably determine the order of satisfaction based on the principles that personal injury compensation claims are preferred over property claims, private law claims are preferred over public law claims, and compensatory claims are preferred over punitive claims. Personal injury compensation arising from the debtor's tortious acts may be satisfied by reference to the order specified in Article 113, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, except for any punitive damages involved. After bankruptcy property is satisfied in the order specified in Article 113 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, if there is a surplus, it may be used in order to satisfy punitive claims such as civil punitive damages, administrative fines, and criminal fines incurred before the acceptance of the bankruptcy application.

29. Establish a mechanism for distinguishing complex and simple cases in bankruptcy case adjudication. People's Courts adjudicating bankruptcy cases shall improve trial efficiency. On the premise of ensuring that the procedural and substantive rights of interested parties are not harmed, a mechanism for distinguishing complex and simple cases in bankruptcy case adjudication shall be established. For bankruptcy cases with clear creditor-debtor relationships and clear debtor property status, the case adjudication process may be accelerated by shortening procedural time and simplifying procedures, but the minimum period stipulated by law shall not be breached.

30. Conclusion of bankruptcy liquidation proceedings. The People's Court's conclusion of bankruptcy liquidation proceedings shall be based on ascertaining the debtor's property status, clarifying the distribution plan for the debtor's property, and ensuring that bankruptcy claims are satisfied according to law. After the acceptance of the bankruptcy application, if upon investigation by the administrator, the debtor's property is insufficient to cover bankruptcy expenses and no one pays or advances payment on its behalf, the People's Court shall, upon the administrator's application, declare bankruptcy and rule to conclude the bankruptcy liquidation proceedings.

31. Restriction on the subrogation right and the right of recourse of the guarantor. Before the conclusion of the bankruptcy proceeding, a guarantor who has already assumed the guarantee liability to the creditor may demand that the debtor transfer to it the portion of the satisfaction that the creditor who has filed a claim would have received in the bankruptcy proceeding. After the conclusion of the bankruptcy proceeding, if the creditor requires the guarantor to assume guarantee liability for the portion not satisfied in the bankruptcy proceeding, the request shall be made within six months after the conclusion of the bankruptcy proceeding. After assuming guarantee liability, the guarantor shall no longer exercise the right of recourse against the debtor that has undergone compromise or reorganization.

VI. Bankruptcy of Affiliated Enterprises

The meeting concluded that when trying bankruptcy cases of affiliated enterprises, people's courts should base their approach on the specific relationship model between the bankrupt affiliated enterprises and adopt different methods for handling them. It is necessary to deal with affiliated relationships where the legal personality is highly confused through substantive consolidation proceedings, ensuring fair repayment to all creditors, while also avoiding improper application of substantive consolidation proceedings that harm the lawful rights and interests of relevant interested parties.

32. Prudent application of substantive consolidation bankruptcy of affiliated enterprises. When trying enterprise bankruptcy cases, people's courts shall respect the independence of the legal personality of enterprises and take as the basic principle the separate determination of the bankruptcy causes of members of affiliated enterprises and the use of separate bankruptcy proceedings. Where there is a high degree of confusion of legal personality among members of affiliated enterprises, the cost of distinguishing the assets of each affiliated enterprise member is excessively high, and the fair repayment interests of creditors are seriously harmed, the substantive consolidation bankruptcy method for affiliated enterprises may be applied as an exception.

33. Review of the application for substantive consolidation. After receiving an application for substantive consolidation, the people's court shall promptly notify the relevant interested parties and organize a hearing; the hearing time shall not be counted in the review period. In the process of reviewing the application for substantive consolidation, the people's court may comprehensively consider factors such as the degree of asset intermingling among affiliated enterprises and its duration, the interest relationships among the enterprises, the overall repayment interests of creditors, and the possibility of increasing the likelihood of enterprise reorganization, and shall make a ruling on whether to conduct substantive consolidation proceedings within thirty days from the date of receipt of the application.

34. Rights remedy for interested parties when a ruling on substantive consolidation is made. If relevant interested parties are dissatisfied with the ruling on substantive consolidation proceedings made by the accepting court, they may apply for reconsideration to the people's court at the next higher level of the accepting court within fifteen days from the date of service of the written ruling.

35. Jurisdiction principle and conflict resolution for substantive consolidation proceedings. Where the substantive consolidation method is used to hear bankruptcy cases of affiliated enterprises, jurisdiction shall lie with the people's court at the place of domicile of the core controlling enterprise among the affiliated enterprises. If the core controlling enterprise is unclear, jurisdiction shall lie with the people's court at the place where the principal assets of the affiliated enterprises are located. If a dispute over jurisdiction arises between multiple courts, they shall report to their common superior people's court for designation of jurisdiction.

36. Legal consequences of substantive consolidation proceedings. Where a people's court rules to adopt the substantive consolidation method to hear a bankruptcy case, the creditor-debtor relationships among the members of the affiliated enterprises shall be extinguished, and the assets of each member shall be merged into a unified bankruptcy estate, which shall be fairly repaid to the creditors of each member in the same proceedings in accordance with the statutory order. Where reorganization is carried out using the substantive consolidation method, the draft reorganization plan shall formulate a unified plan for classification of claims, adjustment of claims, and repayment of claims.

37. Continued existence of enterprise members after substantive consolidation proceedings. Where bankruptcy liquidation is conducted applying the substantive consolidation rules, after the conclusion of the bankruptcy proceedings, each member of the affiliated enterprises shall be dissolved. Where composition or reorganization is conducted applying the substantive consolidation rules, the affiliated enterprises shall in principle be merged into one enterprise. If, according to the composition agreement or reorganization plan, it is genuinely necessary to maintain the independence of an individual enterprise, it shall be handled separately in accordance with the relevant rules on division of enterprises.

38. Coordinated proceedings and jurisdiction principle for bankruptcy cases of affiliated enterprises. Where multiple members of affiliated enterprises all have bankruptcy causes but do not meet the conditions for substantive consolidation, the people's court may, upon application by relevant subjects, conduct coordinated proceedings for multiple bankruptcy proceedings, and may, according to the needs of procedural coordination, comprehensively considering factors such as the efficiency of bankruptcy case proceedings, the order of filing bankruptcy applications, the size of the liabilities of the members, and the place of domicile of the core controlling enterprise, have the common superior court designate one court to exercise centralized jurisdiction.

39. Legal consequences of coordinated proceedings. Coordinated proceedings do not extinguish the creditor-debtor relationships among members of affiliated enterprises, nor do they merge the assets of the members of affiliated enterprises; creditors of each member of the affiliated enterprises shall still be repaid lawfully within the limits of the assets of that enterprise member. However, claims arising from improper use of affiliated relationships among members of affiliated enterprises shall be subordinated to the order of repayment of other ordinary claims, and such subordinated creditors shall not enjoy priority repayment from specific assets provided by other members of the affiliated enterprises.

VII. Connection between Execution Proceedings and Bankruptcy Proceedings

The effective connection between execution proceedings and bankruptcy proceedings is a powerful means to comprehensively advance bankruptcy adjudication work and an important measure to solve the "difficulty in execution." People's courts at all levels must deeply understand the significance of the transfer from execution to bankruptcy, vigorously promote the entry into bankruptcy proceedings of execution cases that meet the conditions for bankruptcy, including cases where execution is impossible, and fully leverage the institutional value of bankruptcy proceedings.

40. Obligations of the executing court to review, inform, explain, and transfer. The execution department must attach great importance to the connection between execution and bankruptcy, and promote the transfer of execution cases that meet the conditions to bankruptcy proceedings. If the executing court finds that an enterprise legal person as the person subject to execution meets the conditions stipulated in Article 2 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, it shall promptly inquire whether the parties agree to transfer the case for bankruptcy review and explain the legal consequences. After the executing court makes a decision to transfer, it shall notify in writing all known executing courts, and all executing courts shall suspend the execution proceedings against the person subject to execution.

41. Transfer and acceptance of cases transferred from execution to bankruptcy. The executing court and the receiving court shall strengthen coordination and cooperation in the transfer process to enhance work effectiveness. When transferring a case, the executing court shall ensure that the materials are complete and the content and form comply with regulations. The receiving court shall carefully review and promptly provide feedback, and shall not refuse to accept or delay case filing without justifiable reason.

42. Lifting of seizure measures or transfer of seized property after acceptance of bankruptcy case. After receiving the bankruptcy acceptance ruling, the executing court shall lift the sealing, seizure, or freezing of the debtor's property; or, upon request of the bankruptcy accepting court, issue a letter transferring the disposal authority over the sealed, seized, or frozen property to the bankruptcy accepting court. The bankruptcy accepting court may, holding the transfer disposal letter from the executing court, proceed to renew the sealing, seizure, or freezing, lift the sealing, seizure, or freezing, or dispose of the property.

If the executing court refuses to lift the sealing, seizure, or freezing measures after receiving the bankruptcy acceptance ruling, the bankruptcy accepting court may request the superior court of the executing court to correct the matter according to law.

43. Information sharing between bankruptcy adjudication departments and execution departments. The bankruptcy accepting court may use the execution inquiry and control system to inquire and control the debtor's property, improving the efficiency of bankruptcy adjudication work, and the execution department shall cooperate.

Courts across the country shall establish the concept of synchronizing online and offline legal procedures, gradually realizing online transfer of execution cases meeting the transfer conditions, enhancing the transparency of the transfer work, and improving the efficiency of case transfer, notification, service, communication, and coordination.

44. Strengthening assessment and management of the work of transfer from execution to bankruptcy. People's courts at all levels shall, based on actual work conditions, establish an assessment mechanism for the work of transfer from execution to bankruptcy, scientifically set assessment indicators, and promote the development of the work of transfer from execution to bankruptcy. Where a court fails to inquire about the parties' opinions when it should, fails to submit for transfer review when it should, or a receiving court refuses to accept the materials for transfer from execution to bankruptcy or refuses to file a case in violation of relevant regulations, in addition to being included in the performance assessment and appraisal system, it shall also be publicly notified and the responsible persons shall be seriously held accountable.

VIII. Information Technology Development for Bankruptcy

The meeting concluded that people's courts at all levels shall further strengthen the information technology development for bankruptcy adjudication, enhance the transparency and credibility of bankruptcy case proceedings, improve the quality and efficiency of bankruptcy case proceedings, and promote enterprise reorganization and revival.

45. Fully leveraging the role of the bankruptcy reorganization case information platform in promoting bankruptcy adjudication work. People's courts at all levels shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Supreme People's Court, standardize the trial of bankruptcy cases through the bankruptcy reorganization case information platform, ensuring full transparency and leaving traces at every step. They shall further strengthen the data statistics, data retrieval, and other functions of the information network, analyze and study the circumstances of enterprise bankruptcy cases, promptly discover new situations, solve new problems, and improve the level of bankruptcy case adjudication.

46. Continuously increasing the disclosure of information in bankruptcy reorganization cases. The content of information disclosed about the debtor enterprise shall be increased to attract potential investors, promote the free flow and effective allocation of factors such as capital, technology, and management capabilities, and help enterprises reorganize and revive. It shall be ensured that creditors and other interested parties promptly and fully understand the progress of the case and the debtor's relevant financial situation, draft reorganization plan, implementation of the reorganization plan, etc., safeguarding the right to know and the right to participate in proceedings of creditors and other interested parties.

47. Using information technology means to improve the quality and efficiency of handling bankruptcy cases. In response to the trend of information technology development, courts shall actively guide the use of online auctions to dispose of bankruptcy assets, enhancing the efficiency of bankruptcy asset disposal. They shall encourage and regulate the convening of creditors' meetings through online means to improve efficiency, reduce bankruptcy costs, and ensure the rights of creditors and other entities to participate in bankruptcy proceedings.

48. Further leveraging the pivotal role of the people's court bankruptcy reorganization case information network. The bankruptcy reorganization case information network shall be continuously improved and promoted. While ensuring timely input of new data into the information network, the filling of existing stock data shall be accelerated, establishing the pivotal role of the information network in enterprise bankruptcy big data, utilizing the information network's publicity and exchange functions, and expanding the initiative of all parties to use the information network.

IX. Cross-Border Bankruptcy

49. Cross-border bankruptcy and the principle of reciprocity. When handling cross-border bankruptcy cases, people's courts shall properly resolve legal conflicts and contradictions in cross-border bankruptcy, and reasonably determine jurisdiction in cross-border bankruptcy cases. Under the principle of equal protection of similar claims, coordinate the balance between the interests of foreign creditors and those of Chinese creditors, and reasonably protect the repayment interests of priority claims such as employee claims and tax claims within China. Actively participate in and promote the negotiation and signing of international treaties on cross-border bankruptcy, explore new methods for applying the principle of reciprocity, strengthen cooperation between Chinese courts and administrators in the field of cross-border bankruptcy, and promote the healthy and orderly development of international investment.

50. Protection of rights and balance of interests in cross-border bankruptcy cases. Carry out cross-border bankruptcy cooperation in accordance with the provisions of Article 5 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law. After a people's court recognizes the judgment or ruling on a bankruptcy case made by a foreign court, after the debtor's assets within the territory of the People's Republic of China have fully satisfied the priority claims such as security interests, employee claims, social insurance costs, and taxes owed within the territory, the remaining assets may be distributed in accordance with the provisions of the foreign court.
